theme: Gluing two things that expand differently
title: Graded Bond-Line Design Under a Thermal-Cycling Edge Concentration
strategies: trivial: uniform softest adhesive type on every segment -- the checker's own reference construction

greedy: uniform maximum-stiffness adhesive on every segment -- individually rational (in the sub-critical size regime this genuinely IS the best uniform choice, and it maximizes each segment's own strength cap too) but the trap: past a size threshold the same uniform stiffness dumps the thermal mismatch strain onto a handful of edge segments whose stress then exceeds their own strength cap, and cycling life collapses toward 0

strong: graded search -- for every candidate soft-edge ramp width and every candidate core stiffness level, evaluate the checker's own stress model directly and keep the best feasible design; softening only the edges (where the mismatch strain concentrates) while keeping the core near maximum stiffness caps the edge stress without giving up the core's static advantage

open ceiling (uncovered): per-segment (non-templated) optimization, asymmetric grading, and joint reasoning across multiple simultaneous cycling profiles -- strong only searches a symmetric two-level-ramp template family
